text:
Maya (Finance): quick follow-up from the postmortem — we agreed on three remediation streams after the token-count spike: 1) root cause + regression guard, 2) invoice fixes & credits, 3) customer comms. can owners confirm timelines?

Owen (Eng): i'm taking the root cause. i think it's the KV cache expiry interaction with our prefixed batching that created duplicate token attribution. will run a focused repro and a small canary fix by EOD tomorrow. assigning to @owen-eng and @liu for code review. :eyeglasses:

Li (Billing): i'll own invoice corrections and credits. plan: generate impacted invoice list, draft credit memo, and run corrections in a controlled batch. target is to finish credits by end of week, but need final impacted-customer list from eng.

Maya (Finance): thanks. Owen — can you provide a query or snippet that produces the affected request ids? billing team needs it to map to invoices.

Owen (Eng): putting the quick query below — it's noisy but should get the subset:

```
SELECT request_id, model, tokens_reported, tokens_actual
FROM token_audit
WHERE event_time BETWEEN '2026-03-10' AND '2026-03-10 23:59:59'
AND tokens_reported - tokens_actual > 50
ORDER BY tokens_reported - tokens_actual DESC
LIMIT 500;
```

Owen (Eng): i'll push the filtered CSV to s3:/redwood-billing/incident/2319991111/impacted_requests.csv in ~2h. li, use that to correlate invoice ids.

Li (Billing): got it — once i have the CSV i will crosswalk to invoices and prepare draft credit memos. quick Q: do we apply credits as line-item adjustments or issue account-level credits? thinking account-level is faster but might upset some customers who need detailed breakdowns.

Sam (Customer Ops): prefer line-item adjustments for enterprise customers on support tier 2+. we can do account-level for small customers. i'll prepare a short template for communications and a cutover schedule. we should also prepare a small FAQ for billing portal.

Maya (Finance): decision: line-item adjustments for invoices > $1k and enterprise. account-credits for <$1k. Sam — please own the comms template and send draft by tomorrow noon. Li — target to open the first correction batch on Thursday morning PST (so support can monitor). Owen — ensure canary fix is deployed before that batch.

Owen (Eng): noted. will also add a regression test to the CI that simulates our prefix+cache behavior so we alert on reoccurrence. ETA for test + small fix: tomorrow EOD.

BillingBot: status_update: impacted_customers_file uploaded to s3 by @owen-eng at 2026-03-11T10:42:00Z; size=124KB; path=s3://redwood-billing/incident/2319991111/impacted_requests.csv

Li (Billing): received the CSV, starting invoice mapping now. will post a short owner+ETA table here once mapping complete.

Maya (Finance): action log (brief):
- Owen (Eng): repro, canary fix, CI regression test — due 2026-03-12 EOD
- Li (Billing): invoice mapping, draft credit memos, first correction batch — start 2026-03-13 AM
- Sam (Customer Ops): customer comms + FAQ drafts — due 2026-03-12 12:00

Maya (Finance): also flagging we should add a recurring monitor for token-delta anomalies (weekly job). Owen — can we add a lightweight alert to PagerDuty if delta rate > 0.5% for a model/day?

Owen (Eng): yes, will add an alert and a Grafana panel for token-delta ratio. i'll post the alert config once live.

Sam (Customer Ops): i'll coordinate with support to triage any inbound billing tickets and will keep a log of affected customers who respond.

Li (Billing): owner+ETA table: will post after mapping but preliminary estimate: ~120 invoices affected, ~45 invoices > $1k. final numbers in ~3h.

Maya (Finance): thanks everyone. i'll track these in the follow-up spreadsheet and sync with legal for any regulatory notes. please update this thread when items complete. :thumbsup:
